The decision worth defending is keeping that logic out of ROS entirely. Its tests run in milliseconds with no ROS process to start, so the nodes we add next stay thin wrappers around code that is already proven, and the workspace is a colcon workspace from the start even though nothing in it talks to ROS yet, because colcon builds plain CMake packages the same way it builds ROS ones, and the ROS packages will sit right next to this one.

c.v: By the end of this session, the Test Bench repository is on GitHub, and a fresh clone builds its first package and runs its tests with

First, the layout. The bench will hold ROS 2 nodes, from the next topic on, and logic that doesn't need ROS: odometry maths, the checks that decide whether a scenario passed, the rules of the supervisor. Put that logic in a plain CMake package with no ROS dependency. Its tests then run in milliseconds without starting any ROS process, and the nodes stay thin wrappers around code that is already tested. colcon builds plain CMake packages as well as ROS 2 ones, so the repository is a colcon workspace from the start:

include(CTest)
if(BUILD_TESTING)
  find_package(GTest REQUIRED)
  include(GoogleTest)
  add_executable(odometry_test test/odometry_test.cpp)
  target_link_libraries(odometry_test PRIVATE bench_core GTest::gtest_main)
  gtest_discover_tests(odometry_test)
endif()

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Builds every package in the workspace and runs every test. Exit code 0 means all passed.
source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
colcon build --cmake-args -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug
colcon test --event-handlers console_cohesion+ --return-code-on-test-failure

c.v: Each line is there for a reason. ROS is sourced before
, because the ROS setup script reads variables that may not be set.
makes the script work from any folder.
prints each package's test output in one piece when it finishes. And
shows the failure in its summary but still exits with 0, so a script or CI can't tell.
colcon also passes a package that has no tests at all without printing anything. Its CMake support first asks
for the list of tests and returns quietly when the list is empty. After you add a package, look at the test output once to see that its tests ran.

items.v: inside the official ROS 2 Jazzy container, so CI and your machine build the same way:

blocks.text:
name: ci
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  build-and-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    container: ros:jazzy-ros-base
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install dependencies
        shell: bash
        run: |
          apt-get update -qq
          rosdep update
          rosdep install --from-paths src --ignore-src -y
      - name: Build and test
        shell: bash
        run: ./check.sh
